observationFocus: Ignore non-board UI such as the mode tabs, score panels, best-score panel, and new-game button unless they help confirm the score changed.
Focus on the 4x4 board state, tile positions, empty spaces, merges, and whether a move changed the board.
When legible, explicitly describe which rows or columns contain tiles, which values are adjacent, and whether a merge or a newly spawned tile appeared after the move.
Track whether the score changed, but do not let the score panel replace direct board understanding.
If the post-move board is still visually ambiguous, say that the board changed but the exact tile layout is still resolving.
Ignore cinematic interpretation and describe the puzzle state directly.
notes: Keep the highest tile anchored in one corner when possible.
Treat each semantic action as a single board shift.
Dynamic/random board updates should be handled one move at a time with a fresh observation after every move.
If a move was verified as successful but the new board is still semantically fuzzy, admit the ambiguity instead of inventing a merge result or a new tile position.
Describe progress in board terms: merge created, new empty cell opened, new tile spawned, or board changed without a fully resolved layout.
